label: Brisnik HR-L1: anticholinergic antidepressant with angle closure glaucoma
title: Anticholinergic antidepressant with angle closure glaucoma
statement: Prescribed anticholinergic antidepressant opipramol, other TCAs (in doses ≥ 50 mg/day), or paroxetine - and the patient has a history of angle closure glaucoma or has developed angle closure glaucoma under treatment

source.document: Brisnik V, et al. Deprescribing of antidepressants: indicators of high-risk and overprescribing. BMC Med 2024;22:193, Tables 3-4
source.citation: Brisnik V, Vukas J, Jung-Sievers C, et al. Deprescribing of antidepressants: development of indicators of high-risk and overprescribing using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. BMC Med 2024;22:193. doi:10.1186/s12916-024-03397-w
source.credit: Brisnik V, Vukas J, Jung-Sievers C, et al. Deprescribing of antidepressants: development of indicators of high-risk and overprescribing using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. BMC Med 2024;22:193. doi:10.1186/s12916-024-03397-w

plain_summary: Paroxetine and opipramol at any dose, and other tricyclics at 50 mg a day or more, can trigger or worsen angle closure glaucoma. Sudden eye pain with redness or worsening vision suggesting an acute attack needs immediate emergency assessment.

medicine_groups.name: Paroxetine and opipramol (any dose)
medicine_groups.note: Opipramol is not sold in Australia, so no brand is listed. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

medicine_groups.name: Other tricyclic antidepressants (count at 50 mg a day or more)
medicine_groups.note: Work out the daily dose from the strength and the directions, for example 25 mg tablets taken as TWO at night is 50 mg a day. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: With paroxetine or opipramol at any dose, or another tricyclic at 50 mg a day or more from strength and directions, cite the supply and evidence of past or on-treatment angle closure glaucoma. A past diagnosis qualifies without implying current disease or an acute attack. A confirmed history of open-angle glaucoma only, or an explicit negative angle closure history, gives no finding. A known Group B dose below 50 mg a day rules out that course alone. If only a Group B course could qualify and the directions leave the threshold unclear, name the missing fact "Prescribed daily dose of the tricyclic antidepressant" unless angle closure has been ruled out. Use the answer only for that medicine and treatment episode. If the dose or the glaucoma history or subtype remains unknown and the other requirement could qualify, report a possible finding and name each missing fact. Name "History of angle-closure glaucoma" when the glaucoma history or subtype is unknown. Name "Prescribed daily dose of the tricyclic antidepressant" when the tricyclic dose could qualify but is unclear. Confirm only with a qualifying supply and glaucoma history, and cite any dose clarification used.

needs_facts.meets: A current or past diagnosis of angle-closure glaucoma qualifies. An unknown subtype remains unresolved. A past diagnosis alone does not establish current disease or an acute attack.

needs_facts.what: Prescribed daily dose of the tricyclic antidepressant
needs_facts.meets: For the tricyclic and treatment episode being reviewed, 50 mg a day or more meets the dose threshold. Below 50 mg a day rules out that course. If the answer is unknown or cannot be linked to that course, its dose remains uncertain.

cannot_be_seen: Whether the person has ever had angle closure glaucoma, what the eye specialist advised, the medicine's real daily use, and any eye drops or procedures done at the hospital or by an eye specialist.
ask_the_gp: Suspected acute angle closure needs immediate emergency assessment. For a stable past diagnosis, could the medicine and the eye specialist's advice be reviewed? If the glaucoma history is unknown, which diagnosis did the eye specialist make?
